title: You Think Humans Hate Risk Equally, Yet One Minus Sign Turns Savers Into Gamblers
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — Daniel Kahneman & Amos Tversky (1979): Prospect Theory, Reference Points & Why Losses Sting Twice as Hard as Gains, grounded in Daniel Kahneman, Amos Tversky (1979) (Econometrica). Empirical findings show that for 241 years since Daniel Bernoulli (1738), economics assumed rational humans judge choices purely by final total wealth ('Expected Utility Theory') regardless of starting point.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how insula, prefrontal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that in their 1979 Econometrica landmark (the most cited paper in economics), psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky tested university cohorts on crisp paired choice problems (Problems 3 and 4, N=95).

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Daniel Kahneman, Amos Tversky (1979). Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk. Econometrica. https://doi.org/10.2307/1914185
- L.Jonathan Cohen (1980). Whose is the fallacy? A rejoinder to Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky. Cognition. https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-0277(80)90017-7
- Alan E. Kazdin (2017). Blending Remarkable Minds, Friendship, and Science: The Story of Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky. PsycCRITIQUES. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0040831

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
